newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower before U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower before U.S. holiday.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday despite a brief intraday bounce ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday which will close trading on COMEX and NYMEX Thursday and Friday.

"The slide lower recently is not surprising, as the strength world stock markets has driven investors out of precious metals, leading funds to add to short positions," Refco New York analyst Jim Steel said.
"Currency movements in South Africa and Australia has also resulted in producer selling for the past three or four nights," he said.
"Ongoing sales of platinum group metals by Russia also added to the weakness in the complex," he said.
COMEX February ended down $1.80 at $375.00 after sliding to a life-of-contract low of $374.50 early.

Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted at $373.10/60 after setting a 20-month low of $372.45 earlier. Gold fixed in London Wednesday afternoon at $373.00, the lowest since January 1995, after closing in New York Tuesday around $374.20/375.20.

News Tuesday that the Russian government has transferred control of precious metal sales to its finance ministry from the old State Committee for Precious Metals led to speculation of gold sales from the Russian central bank, and contributed to the bearish sentiment, traders said.

News last week that Switzerland may abolish its quasi-gold standard, by removing the requirement the country hold gold reserves equal to 40 pct of its currency in circulation, continued to add a bearish tone also, analysts said.

The continued slide in the price of gold in South African rand terms and in Australian dollars was contributing to reports of year end producer hedging from some of the world's largest gold miners in those countries, traders said.

Spot gold has fallen from a multi-year high around 1800 rand an ounce to around 1700 rand in the past four weeks, while in Australian dollars gold has fallen from around $485 an ounce mid-November to $460 Wednesday.
One other factor Wednesday was the ongoing roll out of December gold and silver contracts which have just entered the delivery period.
On the first delivery day for December gold Wednesday, deliveries numbered 5,282 lots, about what was expected, traders said.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.70 at $373.00 after hitting a new contract low of $372.50 early.

Open interest in December gold fell 17,763 lots to 17,847 lots Tuesday, while February open interest jumped 12,729 lots to 86,140, but total gold open interest slipped 3,220 lots to 191,221 contracts.
COMEX March silver ended unchanged at $4.785 but not before setting a contract low of $4.735. Silver slipped to fix at $4.740, its lowest since March 29, 1995, in London Wednesday morning.

On the charts, all four metals in the precious metals complex remain in their downtrends since at least mid-October, analysts noted, but most have again neared oversold levels around on a standard nine-day relative strength index (RSI), analysts noted.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $2.80 at $379.80, just off the new contract low at $379.50 set at the opening. Platinum fixed at $377.75 an ounce in London overnight, the lowest since Dec 8, 1993.
NYMEX March palladium closed down $0.70 at $116.50, and also set a contract low of $116.00. Palladium fixed at $114.75, the lowest since April 20, 1993, in London overnight.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
